selfcare_task_foot_inspection_desc: Check both feet for cuts, blisters, redness or swelling.
selfcare_task_wash_dry_desc: Use lukewarm water and dry well, especially between the toes.
selfcare_task_moisturize_desc: Apply cream to keep skin soft — but not between the toes.
selfcare_task_footwear_desc: Check shoes for objects and wear well-fitting, protective footwear.
selfcare_task_wound_check_desc: Inspect any wound or dressing and keep it clean and dry.
selfcare_do_1: Keep your blood sugar as close to target as possible — take your medication as directed, see your doctor regularly, eat a healthy diet, and make healthy lifestyle changes.
selfcare_do_2: Inspect every part of your feet daily for cuts, sores, blisters, or areas of redness and warmth. Tell your healthcare provider about any changes.
selfcare_do_3: Wash your feet daily with warm water and mild soap, then pat them dry gently — paying special attention to the area between the toes.
selfcare_do_4: Wear loose-fitting cotton socks, and change your socks every day.
selfcare_do_5: Wear shoes with a wide toe box that match the shape of your foot, and choose comfortable, non-tight footwear.
selfcare_do_6: Get regular foot exams, and ask your doctor to check your feet at least once a year.
selfcare_do_7: Take care when trimming your nails: cut them straight across and use a nail file to smooth sharp edges.
selfcare_do_8: Moisturize your feet regularly with a good cream, but avoid applying it between the toes.
selfcare_dont_3: Don't use heating pads or hot-water bottles on your feet, and don't step into a hot bath before testing the water temperature with your elbow first.
selfcare_dont_4: Don't peel or remove dead skin from your feet, cut ingrown toenails yourself, or try to open blisters.
selfcare_dont_5: Don't treat infections or wounds with herbs or unknown remedies.
selfcare_dont_6: Don't soak your feet in water for long periods, and don't use strong disinfectants to sterilize your feet.

consent_v1_body: Your answers help us evaluate how usable this app is. Taking part is voluntary, there are no right or wrong answers, and you may stop at any time. Your responses are anonymous, are not linked to your medical data, and are stored only on this device unless you choose to export them.
consent_v2_body:
Please read this carefully before continuing.

What is collected: your wound scans and measurements, the daily records you enter (blood glucose, medication, self-care, appointments, well-being), your questionnaire answers, and how you use the app.

Where it goes: this information is sent to the DiaFootCare server over an encrypted connection. It is stored under your account, which means it is linked to your identity and to your medical records. It is not anonymous.

Who sees it: the clinical and research team running this study, through a secure dashboard.

What it is used for: to provide your care, to improve the app, and as data in a usability and clinical study.

Responses already on this device: if you have answered questionnaires before today, those answers were collected under an earlier declaration that said they would stay on this device. By accepting below, you agree that those earlier answers may also be sent to the server and used in the same way. If you do not want that, do not accept — contact the study team instead.

Accepting is required to use DiaFootCare during the study period. You may withdraw at any time by contacting the study team, who will stop further collection and can remove your data on request. Withdrawing does not affect the care you receive.
consent_accept_label: I have read and understood the above, and I agree.
consent_required_notice: You need to accept this declaration to continue using DiaFootCare.
consent_decline_explain: DiaFootCare cannot be used without accepting the data-sharing declaration during the study period. You can review it again at any time from your profile.
consent_updated_notice: Our data-sharing declaration has changed. Please review it.

Learn how to protect your feet.
edu_subtitle: Learn simple, expert-backed ways to protect your feet.
edu_ask_intro: Your pharmacist is an easy-to-reach expert. Consider asking:
edu_ask_q1: Do any of my medicines affect my blood sugar or healing?
edu_ask_q2: Which moisturizers or foot-care products suit diabetic skin?
edu_ask_q3: How should I store and use my wound dressings?
edu_disclaimer: This is general guidance, not a substitute for your care team's advice.
edu_pharm_1: Ask your pharmacist to review all your medicines for any that affect blood sugar or circulation.
edu_pharm_2: Choose a fragrance-free, urea-based moisturizer for dry diabetic skin.
edu_pharm_3: Keep a small foot-care kit: a mirror, mild soap, moisturizer, and clean dressings.
edu_pharm_4: Never treat corns or calluses with over-the-counter acid removers — they can cause ulcers.
edu_foot_care_summary: Simple daily habits that protect your feet.
edu_foot_care_intro: Checking and caring for your feet every day is the single best way to catch small problems before they turn serious.
edu_foot_care_b1: Inspect the tops, soles, and between your toes daily — use a mirror or ask for help to see the soles.
edu_foot_care_b2: Wash your feet in lukewarm water with mild soap, then dry gently, especially between the toes.
edu_foot_care_b3: Moisturize dry skin, but not between the toes where extra moisture can cause skin breakdown.
edu_foot_care_b4: Trim nails straight across and smooth sharp edges with a file; never cut into the corners.
edu_foot_care_b5: Never use sharp tools, corn removers, or heat on your feet — see a professional instead.
edu_footwear_summary: Shoes and socks that prevent pressure and injury.
edu_footwear_intro: Well-fitting footwear spreads pressure evenly and shields your feet from injuries you might not feel.
edu_footwear_b1: Choose shoes with a wide, deep toe box that matches the shape of your foot.
edu_footwear_b2: Always check inside your shoes for stones, seams, or objects before putting them on.
edu_footwear_b3: Break in new shoes gradually, and never walk barefoot — even indoors.
edu_footwear_b4: Wear seamless, cushioned cotton or wool socks and change them every day.
edu_footwear_b5: Ask about custom insoles or diabetic footwear if you have areas of high pressure.
edu_blood_sugar_intro: High blood sugar slows healing and weakens your defenses against infection. Keeping glucose near target protects your feet.
edu_blood_sugar_b1: Take your medications exactly as prescribed and keep your regular check-ups.
edu_blood_sugar_b2: Aim for the blood-sugar targets your care team set for you.
edu_blood_sugar_b3: Log your readings so you and your clinician can spot trends early.
edu_blood_sugar_b4: Balanced meals, regular activity, and not smoking all improve circulation and healing.
edu_warning_signs_title: Warning Signs: When to Seek Help
edu_warning_signs_intro: Some changes need same-day medical attention. When in doubt, contact your care team.
edu_warning_signs_b1: Redness, warmth, swelling, or pus around a wound — possible infection.
edu_warning_signs_b2: A new cut, blister, or ulcer that doesn't start healing within a few days.
edu_warning_signs_b3: Skin that turns dark, blue, or black, or a cold and painful foot — possible poor blood flow.
edu_warning_signs_b4: Fever or feeling unwell together with a foot wound.
edu_warning_signs_b5: New numbness, tingling, or pain that is unusual for you.
edu_wound_care_title: Caring for a Wound or Dressing
edu_wound_care_intro: Good wound hygiene gives your body the best chance to heal and helps prevent infection.
edu_wound_care_b1: Follow your clinician's instructions for cleaning and changing dressings.
edu_wound_care_b2: Keep the wound clean and dry, and wash your hands before and after care.
edu_wound_care_b3: Don't remove dead skin, pop blisters, or apply unproven remedies yourself.
edu_wound_care_b4: Offload pressure from the wound — use prescribed footwear or aids and rest the foot.
edu_wound_care_b5: Take photos to track healing and share them at your appointments.

terms_intro: By using this application, you agree to the following terms and conditions:
terms_1_b: This app is designed to assist users in tracking wound healing and related health data. It is not intended to replace professional medical advice.

senior_tip_1_t: Use the App in a Well-Lit Area
senior_tip_1_b: Make sure the room is well-lit to see the screen clearly and avoid eye strain.
senior_tip_2_b: If reading is difficult, go to Settings → Display → Increase Font Size.
senior_tip_3_b: The app is designed to be simple. Don’t rush—each screen has clear buttons and large icons.
senior_tip_4_b: If you prefer listening, you can enable voice guidance to help you through the app.
senior_tip_5_b: Invite a trusted caregiver to help you review reminders and notes when needed.
senior_tip_6_b: Review app notifications each day for reminders or important updates.
senior_tip_7_b: You can always edit or delete entries—take your time and tap carefully.
